key_insight: For a natural class of nonconvex objectives, SGD with learning rate decay provably needs exponentially fewer gradient queries for global optimization than any fixed learning rate in the small-step-size regime.
engineering_relevance: The result gives theoretical support for decaying learning rates when using SGD to seek global optima in nonconvex engineering models.
method: Analyze a nonconvex function class containing many popular benchmark objectives.
Compare gradient-query complexity of decaying-rate SGD with fixed-rate SGD.
Use weak Poincaré inequalities to prove polynomial-time annealing for an associated non-logconcave sampling task.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity guarantees rather than numerical experiments or dataset evaluations.
watch_item: The exponential separation applies to the analyzed function class and small-step-size fixed-rate baselines, not necessarily to arbitrary objectives or practical training settings.
paper_title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
